item.content:encoded:

🎙
Remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at the Plenary Session of the 8th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum
(Moscow, October 27, 2026)
Key points
:
• When it was established 25 years ago,
the Gas Exporting Countries Forum
(
#GECF
) was conceived as a platform for expert analysis, sharing experience, and assessing and forecasting developments in the gas market.
This is precisely how our dialogue has evolved – without any backroom intrigue or attempts to manipulate the market
.
•
GECF countries account for 70% of the world’s natural gas reserves and around 40% of global gas exports.
Our countries thus make a significant contribution to global energy security and the balanced development of countries and macroregions.
• Today, gas accounts for a quarter of the global energy mix. In 2025, consumption rose by 1.2% to 4.2 trillion cubic metres. These trends are expected to continue.
The role of natural gas as a mainstay of global energy, industry, agriculture and international trade will only grow.
•
Russia is a key player in the global gas market. We rank first in the world in natural gas reserves and second in production.
We have built a unique production complex that enables us to diversify gas supplies and develop gas processing and gas-based chemical production.
•
The situation in the Middle East
has deteriorated. Russian gas pipelines to Europe have been subjected to outright terrorist attacks –
they were blown up
. Some countries have also imposed barriers to purchasing equipment and technology for the sector.
As a result, the global gas industry faces uncertainty.
❗️
Any attempts to exclude Russia from the global gas market or hold back the development of our gas industry have serious consequences
, above all in the form of rising, exorbitant costs for end users abroad – companies, industrial enterprises and households.
•
Europe is undermining its own industry and social sector by rejecting Russian energy supplies and terminating long-term contracts.
There is a Russian saying:
“Do not dig a pit for someone else, or you may fall into it yourself”
. In my view, this is precisely what has happened in EU countries.
• To address the challenges facing the global gas industry,
we must strengthen cooperation, rather than erect barriers
, particularly among gas-exporting countries. We must build on our own capabilities and sovereign technologies, developing open, trust-based cooperation founded on mutual benefit and respect for each other’s interests.
• GECF, its members and observers have the resources and capabilities to tackle the most complex challenges in the gas industry and across the global energy sector.
For its part, Russia stands ready to make a substantial contribution to this work.

item.title: 🗓 #Announcement On October 28-29, the Third Russia – Africa Summit will take place in Moscow under
item.description: #Announcement 🗓 On October 28-29, the Third Russia – Africa Summit will take place in Moscow under the chairmanship of Russia's President Vladimir Putin and Chairperson of the African Union, President of Burundi Evariste Ndayishimiye . Representatives of almost 50 African countries will take part in the Summit , including Heads of State and Government as well as Leaders of the continent’s integration associations. The focus will be on the further development of Russia’s multifaceted ties with African nations in politics, trade and the economy, investment, science and technology, and humanitarian and cultural affairs. ✍️ The Summit is expected to adopt: • a final declaration; • the next Russia – Africa Partnership Forum Action Plan for 2027-2029; • the Declaration of Cooperation in the Civilian Application of Artificial Intelligence Technologies; • a substantial package of intergovernmental and interdepartmental agreements covering cooperation between Russia and Africa in a wide range of areas. On October 28, the Leaders of Russia and Burundi will address the Russia – Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum , which will bring together Russian and African officials, representatives of government agencies, business and expert communities. In addition, Vladimir Putin will hold a meeting with Leaders of Africa’s regional organisations . 🤝 Russia's President will hold a series of bilateral talks with heads of African states on the sidelines of the Summit . 👉 LEARN MORE 👉 BUSINESS PR

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/33003

🎙
Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman
Maria Zakharova
’s
answer
to a media question about the situation surrounding
ZNPP
(October 26, 2026)
❓
Question: The Kiev regime has stepped up the attacks on the Zaporozhskaya Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) and the satellite town of Energodar, which fact has significantly destabilised the operation of the ZNPP. How would you comment on these attacks?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
The Kiev authorities completely lost their minds and
intensified targeted attacks on the
#ZNPP
and the satellite town of Energodar
, which is home to the plant’s personnel, who continue to perform their duties heroically under extremely challenging conditions, as do their families.
Earlier this week,
the Ukrainian forces targeted exclusively civilian sites,
namely, an art school and the Russian Emergencies Ministry’s fire and rescue unit. Clearly, unable to strike the ZNPP directly, the Kiev regime continues its futile attempts to destabilise the plant’s operations by
intimidating its personnel.
Such criminal actions clearly show that the sole true objective of Zelensky and his junta is
to multiply the number of casualties
and turn the Zaporozhye Region into a barren land of radioactive contamination.
Having failed the test of their own competence, the former actors continue to labour under the delusion that any criticism, or even condemnation, amounts to publicity that can be monetised.
It is time for the Western patrons and sponsors of this deranged clique, to whom they have effectively given carte blanche to get away with any crimes, to realise that they are dumping their money not merely in a failed anti-Russia project, but also in
creating direct radiological threats in the heart of Europe,
including to their own citizens.
We are compelled to note that international bodies, above all the
#IAEA
,
have reacted with considerable restraint to Kiev’s provocative antics
and have yet to muster the courage to identify Ukraine directly as the culprit. Apparently, they fail to appreciate that such spineless behaviour could lead to catastrophe.
❗️
For our part,
we consistently bring detailed information about Ukraine’s outrages to the attention of the international public
, including at relevant international forums, and spare no effort to protect the ZNPP, its personnel, and the people of Energodar from Kiev’s attacks.
